findings.ACCEPTANCE TEST: Each supported tag type is physically read by the app on the target device and converted without errors, with warnings handled.
findings.CONSEQUENCE: Actual Android NFC-A/NFC-V RF behavior, NDEF parsing, tag memory layout, and read success on real tags remain unverified, potentially leading to field failures or unsupported tags.
findings.EVIDENCE: objective_evidence.physical_external_tags.OpenTag3D = 'NOT RUN - no physical formatted tag supplied'; OpenPrintTag = 'NOT RUN - no physical NFC-V tag supplied'; known_limits states no physical tag was available, radio-path acceptance remains open.
findings.FINDING: OpenTag3D and OpenPrintTag read-only conversion has not been validated against any physical tag hardware. The device test suite only exercises adapter code; official hardware/fixtures were not used.
findings.REQUIRED CORRECTION: Execute acceptance tests with official OpenTag3D/OpenPrintTag physical tags or certified fixtures before release; include real NFC interaction.

findings.ACCEPTANCE TEST: Live sync against real Spoolman server passes all existing mock test scenarios and no unexpected 4xx/5xx occur.
findings.CONSEQUENCE: Actual API contract, authentication (if any), TLS, error handling, and server-side behavior at the pinned revision are unverified, risking sync failures or data corruption in production.
findings.EVIDENCE: objective_evidence.live_spoolman_server = 'NOT RUN - no server URL supplied; mock transport create/update/failure tests pass'; known_limits states no live Spoolman server URL was supplied.
findings.FINDING: Spoolman profile sync has only been tested against mocks; no real Spoolman server interaction was performed.
findings.REQUIRED CORRECTION: Run sync tests against a pinned Spoolman server revision (or recorded HTTP interactions) covering create, update, failure, and edge cases.

findings.ACCEPTANCE TEST: Simulate dropped response after server mutation; verify no duplicate records and local state eventually matches server or user is prompted.
findings.CONSEQUENCE: If a create/update request is committed server-side but the response is lost, the client may report failure and retry, causing duplicate profiles; or may report success without knowing server state, leading to inconsistent local/remote state.
findings.EVIDENCE: architecture_decisions item: 'Mutation transport loss is UNKNOWN and never automatically retried'; no idempotency or reconciliation mechanism is mentioned.
findings.FINDING: Mutation transport loss is explicitly UNKNOWN and is never automatically retried, so partial failures can produce duplicates or false failure/success.
findings.REQUIRED CORRECTION: Implement idempotent operations (client-generated ID or conflict-free update) and/or automatic retry with response validation; or clearly surface uncertain status and provide manual reconciliation.

findings.ACCEPTANCE TEST: All preserved records match expected content exactly after installation, import, and conversion.
findings.CONSEQUENCE: Silent corruption, field truncation, or incorrect conversion could occur while counts remain identical, giving false confidence in preservation.
findings.EVIDENCE: objective_evidence.data_preservation shows counts (e.g., custom_records 6->6, filament_profiles 6->6, physical_spools 6->6, tag_bindings 1->1), but no content equality or checksum evidence is provided.
findings.FINDING: Data preservation evidence consists only of entity counts before/after, not content integrity; no hashes or field-level comparison are reported.
findings.REQUIRED CORRECTION: Add content-level verification (e.g., compare serialized fields, hashes, or key attributes) for all preserved datasets and report results.

findings.ACCEPTANCE TEST: Non-local HTTP configuration is blocked or requires explicit user warning; local loopback HTTP remains permitted.
findings.CONSEQUENCE: If a user points the app at a remote Spoolman instance over HTTP, all sync traffic (profiles, potential metadata) is unencrypted and susceptible to interception or tampering.
findings.EVIDENCE: architecture_decisions item: 'Cleartext HTTP is enabled for local Spoolman prototypes and disclosed; no Spoolman credentials are handled'.
findings.FINDING: Cleartext HTTP is enabled for Spoolman connections; although disclosed and no credentials handled, synced profile data may be exposed if a non-local server is configured.
findings.REQUIRED CORRECTION: Restrict cleartext HTTP to loopback/private addresses only, or enforce HTTPS for non-local endpoints and show prominent warning before allowing insecure connections.

findings.ACCEPTANCE TEST: After sync, physical spool data is either synced or the user is explicitly informed of the limitation without data loss.
findings.CONSEQUENCE: Users may expect full two-way sync of all data, but physical spools remain unsynced, leading to data divergence or confusion.
findings.EVIDENCE: architecture_decisions item: 'Live sync is profile-only and uses stable external IDs; physical spool creation is excluded because Spoolman has no spool external ID'; objective_evidence.data_preservation shows 6 physical_spools preserved, but no sync path for them.
findings.FINDING: Live sync deliberately excludes physical spool creation because Spoolman has no spool external ID, but the objective includes Spoolman sync and import/export may cover physical spools.
findings.REQUIRED CORRECTION: If not supported, clearly communicate this limitation in UI/docs; otherwise explore a stable local mapping or Spoolman spool ID mapping to enable sync.
